The folder layout mirrors three's examples/jsm, so GLTFLoader's relative import
"../utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js" resolves unchanged. meshopt_decoder.module.js is
meshoptimizer's decoder (MIT, Arseny Kapoulkine) as shipped inside three; it has no
imports. It decodes EXT_meshopt_compression, which ../models/cubesat-3u.glb uses.

GLTFLoader.js and BufferGeometryUtils.js import the bare specifier "three". Every page
that loads them (directly or through ../satellite.js) must declare an import map
before its first module script, pointing "three" at the same file the rest of the
page uses so there is only one copy of three.js:

  site/explore/index.html          {"imports": {"three": "../globe/vendor/three.module.min.js"}}
  site/explore/dev/satellite.html  {"imports": {"three": "../../globe/vendor/three.module.min.js"}}

e.g.
  <script type="importmap">
    { "imports": { "three": "../globe/vendor/three.module.min.js" } }
  </script>

Modules that import three by relative URL instead of "three" still share the instance
as long as both resolve to the same absolute URL.
